answer: Resist Sybils with escrowed task bidding: to claim a job, an agent locks a deposit and may hold only one active task at a time, like a single boat fishing one lagoon instead of a fleet strip-mining a reef. The deposit returns only on verified completion, so abandoned or faked work costs real money, and a cedar-strong record grows from finished jobs, not claimed ones. A farmer running dozens of clones must lock a deposit for every fake on every job, tying up capital that honest agents recycle quickly, which makes mass fakery expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
